snippet.title: ASA Therizinosaurus TLC Trailer
snippet.description:
Therizinosaurus is now stepping up for its turn in the TLC spotlight!

Thanks to your Extra Life vote, one of ARK's most iconic creatures is getting a fresh coat of feathers, all while staying true to the role Survivors have relied on for years. Rather than redefining the creature, this TLC focuses on improving combat responsiveness, controls, traversal, visual progression and expanding the creature’s personality. 

The Therizino has always had a reputation for turning an innocent stroll through the woods into a frantic sprint for your life, and that isn't changing anytime soon. Survivors will find that wild ones are a little more patient than they used to be. They now make their intentions crystal clear, fixing you with an unblinking stare, spreading those infamous claws, and giving you one last chance to reconsider your life choices. Whether you heed that warning is entirely up to you.

Thank you again to everyone who supported Extra Life and helped bring this TLC to life. Next stop, Giganotosaurus!

snippet.title: Dimitri Vegas, Bountyhunter, BRANDON - Woops (Official Music Video)
snippet.description:
Listen to Dimitri Vegas, Bountyhunter, BRANDON - Woops:
https://orcd.co/_woops

After months of appearing in sets throughout clubs and festival stages the world over, Dimitri Vegas, Bountyhunter and BRANDON finally release their hotly anticipated collaboration ‘Woops’ via Smash The House.
 
‘Woops’ has spent months picking up support from seemingly every corner of electronic music. It emerged as the #1 most-played track at both Ultra and Tomorrowland in 2026, underlining the unusual reach the track has already found.
 
The laundry list of DJs who have put ‘Woops’ into rotation is as varied as it is extensive. Anyma, Solomun, Dom Dolla, Charlotte de Witte, Amelie Lens, Vintage Culture, Eli Brown, Odd Mob, Chris Lake, Cloonee, Cassian, Miss Monique, Nico Moreno, Novah, Lilly Palmer, Kevin de Vries, CamelPhat and many others, are among those supporting it from the underground, while at the other end of the electronic spectrum, Swedish House Mafia, Tiësto, The Chainsmokers, Armin van Buuren, Oliver Heldens, Diplo, and Afrojack have also been hammering the track, turning ‘Woops’ into a bona fide crossover between underground dancefloors and festival mainstages.
 
But the story extends well beyond the DJ booth. The ‘Woops’ phenomenon has generated billions of views and hundreds of thousands of creations on TikTok, tens of millions of YouTube views and more than 500,000 Shazams. With over 100 million total streams behind it, ‘Woops’ has also remained a presence in Beatport’s Hard Dance Top 100 for years, regularly climbing back into the Top 10.
